title: Cost rates
hint: Every number on the cost pages is computed from these rates.

warn.title: A wrong rate raises no error
warn.body: It just makes the whole cost report quietly wrong, and people use that report to make downsizing and budget decisions. Also: when region+machine family finds no rate, the cost falls back to the default tier — the number looks perfectly normal but the price may not be right. The cost overview page now flags how many hosts were priced that way and which regions lack rates.

section.nodesHint: Shows only what needs attention: manually overridden, and no matching rate. Covers K8s nodes only — non-node VMs are not checked here

field.regionHint: Must match the cloud's region code, e.g. asia-east1. A typo raises no error — hosts in that region just never match a rate and get priced from the default tier, so the cost looks normal while using another region's price.
field.familyHint: The family prefix, e.g. n2, e2, c3. Matched by prefix, so n2-standard-8 is not needed.
field.diskTypeHint: For example pd-balanced or pd-ssd, matching the cloud disk type code.

dialog.desc: Rates come from the cloud provider's price list. Reconcile against an invoice before changing them rather than guessing.

empty.computeReason: There is not a single compute rate in the table (not even a default tier), so compute cost for every host and node is counted as 0 — the cost page will look like "these machines are free" rather than "rates are not configured yet". Configure at least a default tier so uncovered regions get a fallback estimate.
empty.diskReason: Storage cost for every disk and PVC is 0. Storage is usually the most under-counted part of the bill.

error.compute: Compute rates could not be loaded
error.disk: Disk rates could not be loaded

nodes.allByRate: All {{count}} K8s nodes are priced from the rate table, with no manual overrides and no unmatched rates
nodes.overrideDesc: Once overridden, this node no longer follows the rate table — later rate changes will not affect it.
nodes.zeroHint: Enter 0 to remove the override and go back to rate-based pricing.
nodes.scopeCaveat: This holds for K8s nodes only. Non-node VMs in the host inventory are outside this check — they are also priced from the rate table, but nothing verifies that they match
nodes.countsExplain: (why does this count differ from the cost overview?)
nodes.countsExplainHint: The three counts use different scopes and are all correct: the cost overview covers the whole host inventory (including non-node VMs); this section reads the K8s node table only; is_k8s_node marks hosts that appear in both. A machine may exist in only one of the two (managed node-pool nodes never enter the host inventory)
